On 25 June 1983 India beat the West Indies at Lord's in London to win the third Cricket World Cup. Few had given the team any chance; India had won just one match in the two earlier tournaments.

The captain was Kapil Dev, a fast bowler from Haryana. In the group stage his 175 not out against Zimbabwe rescued India from 17 for 5. In the final India made only 183, but the bowlers dismissed the West Indies, who had won the first two cups, for 140.

The win changed Indian sport. Cricket, already popular, became a national passion and a business, as live colour television spread through the 1980s. India and Pakistan hosted the next World Cup in 1987, the first held outside England. The money and audience that followed made India the centre of world cricket and led, in time, to the Indian Premier League. Sri Lanka's surprise win in 1996 echoed it; see Sri Lanka wins Cricket World Cup.
